summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue fell 13.3% to INR1,167 crore, but PAT rose to INR58 crore; INR700 crore contingency provision taken from free reserves.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR1,167 crore (down 13.3% YoY), with EBITDA of about INR116 crore (~10% margin) and PAT of INR58 crore (5% margin, up 206 bps YoY). FY26 revenue fell 14% to INR4,377 crore, EBITDA was INR450 crore (10.2% margin) and PAT INR194 crore (4.4%). The company created a INR700 crore contingency provision charged to free reserves, which led to a qualified auditor report; management says it has no cash impact. Management also outlined a "Texmaco 2.0" Vision 2030 plan targeting 2x top line and mid-teen-plus EBITDA margins, and disclosed a large South Africa wagon and locomotive order (about INR4,000 crore) with delivery by FY28.

financial_highlights.change: Charged to free reserves; no cash impact
FY26 lower than record prior year

financial_highlights.value: 8,964 MT in Q4 FY26; ~34,000 MT in FY26

segments.name: Railways / wagons (Kalindee)
segments.commentary: Freight car deliveries of 2,196 in Q4 and 8,372 in FY26 were hit by wheel-set availability and global supply chain issues. Management says about 70% of the wagon order book is from private customers.

segments.name: Bright Power (electrification)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 66% to INR610 crore in FY26 with a 10.8% EBIT margin; management called the growth phenomenal for the future.

segments.name: Foundry
segments.commentary: Volume was 8,964 MT in Q4 and about 34,000 MT for FY26, with the year affected by supply chain disruptions and US tariffs.

segments.name: Defence / digital / real estate (new verticals)
segments.commentary: Board approved INR200 crore capex for defence; envelope for overall new-business capex cited at INR1,500-2,000 crore. A real estate division is being set up around surplus land, and the Invariz.ai GCC is being built as a future commercial AI service.

guidance_outlook: Management expects top-line and bottom-line growth in FY27 versus FY26, but declined to give specific revenue or EBITDA numbers.
Vision 2030 / Texmaco 2.0 targets doubling top line and EBITDA margins in the mid-teens or above, to be achieved in 12-36 months.
Management expects part of the INR700 crore contingency provision to be released as claims are realised and visibility on contracts improves.
Capex for new businesses is expected to be within INR1,500-2,000 crore, to be disclosed progressively; net debt-to-equity is expected to stay below about 0.2.
Management expects the South Africa order (about 2,200 wagons, 30 diesel locomotives, 15-year maintenance) to be delivered by FY28, with revenue largely in FY28 per management's answer.
Management expects a wagon requirement of about 25,000-30,000 over 5-7 years, plus replacement demand of 10,000-14,000 per year.
capex_capacity: Board approved INR200 crore capex for the defence business; total new-business capex envelope estimated at INR1,500-2,000 crore.
Management says it makes about 11 types of wagons and has a track record in 16 countries across multiple gauges.
Management says the company is moving from vehicle-count metrics to a volume-to-value approach.
Finance cost of about INR120 crore for the year includes bank guarantee commission charges, not just interest.
demand_pricing: South Africa order: about INR4,000 crore, 2,200 wagons and 30 diesel locomotives by FY28, including a 15-year maintenance component. Pricing covers the full life cycle.
Management declined to say whether the South Africa order has raw material pass-through or is fixed price, citing its envelope structure and localisation.
Management expects a Indian Railways wagon tender of 1.5-2 lakh wagons in the near term, but has not yet seen bids called.
Private-sector wagon market share is about 40-45%, with private demand estimated at 12,000-15,000 wagons a year on a consistent basis.
Management named Europeans and Chinese competitors in international bids, along with local competitors.
Wheel-set availability is currently adequate with Indian Railways capacity, but a policy decision on imports remains open.

qa_highlights.question: What visibility is there on new Indian Railways wagon orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no bids have been called yet, but expects 1.5-2 lakh wagons in the near term, with the first stage of about 1.3-1.4 lakh wagons already awarded in 2022-23.

qa_highlights.question: Is the South Africa order mostly FY28 revenue, and is FY27 softer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue will largely come in FY28 as things stand, and also reiterated that it expects top-line and bottom-line growth in FY27 versus FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is needed for the new businesses and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Defence capex of INR200 crore has been approved; the overall envelope is INR1,500-2,000 crore, to be updated as projects progress, and management expects leverage to stay within range.

qa_highlights.question: Who will build the locomotives for the South Africa order, and what is the pricing structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has accepted the award but could not disclose the locomotive partner or pricing structure yet, citing disclosure constraints.

qa_highlights.question: What are the defence plans and when is the first commercial order expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said technology tie-ups are at an advanced stage in areas such as autonomous vehicles, could not disclose specifics, and expects a positive step within this financial year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scope and timing of the wagon tender from Indian Railways?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 25,000-30,000 wagons over 5-7 years, which may come in one go or in tranches, but could not give a timing for the tender.

risks_watch: INR700 crore contingency provision charged to free reserves; the statutory auditor has qualified the report. Watch for release of the provision as claims are realised.
Heavy reliance on large claims that are pending with customers; management asked for patience on timing.
Wheel-set supply and any government decision on imports could constrain wagon output.
Timing of the Indian Railways wagon tender remains uncertain; management could not give a date.
Management declined to give FY27 guidance numbers and gave limited disclosure on the South Africa locomotive scope, pricing and partner.
Execution risk on new verticals (defence, real estate, Invariz.ai GCC, metro) and the INR1,500-2,000 crore capex envelope.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the long-term vision and the South Africa order, but cautious and evasive on near-term numbers, locomotive pricing, FY27 guidance and the timing of the wagon tender. Management repeatedly cited confidentiality constraints and deferred detail to later updates.
key_quotes: I must tell you that this has no cash impact because of this provision.
The company believes that this contingency provision is a maximum potential risk under the worst-case scenario.
We cannot be too specific for a forward-looking statement.
So there will be a requirement about 25,000 to 30,000 wagon for the coming 5 to 7 years.

adds.what: INR200 crore defence business capex (board approved); part of INR1,500-2,000 crore new-business capex envelope

growth.why: Management expects revenue and profit growth in FY27 but gave no numbers; backing is a large South Africa order (about INR4,000 crore, 2,200 wagons and 30 locomotives, delivery by FY28) and a INR200 crore defence capex approval, with the Vision 2030 2x top-line target set over 12-36 months.
